title: The Multi-League Talent Pipeline: How Delhi Capitals Could Scout Globally
dek: IPL squads draw on a global market fed by leagues around the world. Where Delhi Capitals source their overseas players, against the league, shows how wide their scouting net is.
excerpt: Since 2024, overseas action in the IPL has come from a measurable set of countries, led by South Africa. Delhi Capitals' largest source is South Africa. A global pipeline means scouting the leagues those players come through.

sections.heading: A Global Market
body: IPL franchises now compete with leagues in South Africa, the Caribbean, Australia, England, the UAE and the United States for overseas talent, and scout through all of them.

sections.heading: Proposal: A Multi-League Pipeline
body: Proposal: scout systematically through the leagues that feed the IPL, using ball-by-ball data from those leagues and the cross-league translation work in this series to rank candidates.

sections.heading: Data Limits
body: Nationality comes from player-bio data and squad lists, covering players who faced or bowled {{ev:ml-cover}} of IPL balls since 2024; squad-list nationality contains known errors. Other leagues' data is not in the warehouse.
Country of birth and country represented can differ; the data uses the latter.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Widen the Net Deliberately
body: Delhi Capitals should compare their overseas sourcing with the league's and scout the leagues behind under-used countries.
Adding other leagues' ball-by-ball data would make that scouting measurable.
